newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber-End of wintering lifts supply, hits prices.
newsitem.headline: Rubber-End of wintering lifts supply, hits prices.

text.p: Southeast Asian rubber prices are seen heading lower near term as supplies rise with the end of a mild wintering season, regional traders said on Monday.
"It doesn't look good," a trader in Bangkok said. "With more supplies looming, prices are likely to drop further."
"Wintering's almost over. May/June, I think we're going to see prices lower," a senior rubber trader in Singapore added. "I think we're a long way from the bottom."
Dealers said this year's wintering season, when rubber trees shed their leaves and latex flow slows, has not been as supportive for prices as usual due to poor consumer demand.
Supplies of rubber to the market this week in Thailand fell 47 percent to 103,612 kg compared with the previous week.
"We're already seeing production picking up with wintering almost done," a dealer for a North American rubber trading firm said. "The market is going to remain in the doldrums."

Last week's announcement by the U.S. National Defense Stockpile Center that it will be offering 13,928.53 long tons of technically specified heavy rubber later this month will put further pressure on prices, traders said.
"That is going to make the situation worse," one trader in Singapore said.
News the Thai government sought 5,000 tonnes of RSS3 grade rubber for July and China was making inquiries in the market failed to lift prices due to weak overall demand, dealers said.
Thai benchmark RSS3 rubber was indicated around 117.00-119.00 US cents a kg FOB Bangkok on Friday against 118.00-119.00 cents the previous week.
In Indonesia, traders said they expect offer prices for benchmark tyre-grade SIR20 to soften further this week as sentiment remains bearish.

"There are no serious buyers in the market and consumer demand is very poor. We expect a bearish trend this week because we don't see any fresh factors which can boost sentiment," one Indonesian trader said.
While supplies are tight in Medan due to wintering, the supply situation in other growing areas was unaffected.

There was some sporadic small-lot buying from European and U.S. buyers, but this failed to support prices. Some traders said they believe most buyers are staying away from the market because of expectations prices will decline further.
Ample supplies on hand made it even more difficult for traders to sell rubber, they said.
"Some traders believe maybe it's time for INRO (International Natural Rubber Organisation) to come to the local market to support prices," a trader in Indonesia said.
INRO could buy Indonesian rubber and then sell it to U.S. and European buyers to help support local prices, he added.
A deal was done on Friday at 49.375 U.S. cents a lb FOB Palembang for June shipment.
Offer prices were stable at 49.25 cents FOB Padang, at 49.50 cents FOB Surabaya and at 49.00 cents FOB Pontianak and Jambi. Offer prices in Medan reached 49.75 cents a lb.
Malaysian rubber prices were also seen moving in a tight range this week, traders said.
"I doubt the market will move much in either direction," a Malaysian trader said.
Another trader said the market would remain bearish this week though losses could be restricted to "one to two cents".

Traders noted some Chinese inquiries for SMR 20 on Friday but nothing was concluded. They said China was asking for a price of 280 cents a kg for April/May shipment, compared with sellers' prices of 282-283 cents.
They expect some offtake from China soon, but the prospects for fresh buying by European and U.S. consumers remain dim.
"(The) supply of raw materials is still not back to normal, so producers are not really keen to sell at current prices," a trader said.

The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted the benchmark RSS1 at 294.50 Malaysian cents a kg for May buyer, down four cents from the previous week, at the close of the market last week. May SMR 20 buyer was quoted at 278.50 cents, against 285 previously.
Drum latex was offered by trading houses almost unchanged at 235 cents a kg on Friday.
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
